# AF 第十章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 10

[P01] YEARS passed. The seasons came and went. A time came when no one remembered the old days before the uprising（起义）, except Clover, Benjamin, Moses the raven（乌鸦）, and some of the pigs; Bluebell, Jessie, and Pincher were dead. Muriel was dead; Bluebell, Jessie, and Pincher were dead. Jones too was dead—he had died in a home for drunks in another part of the country. Snowball was forgotten. Boxer was forgotten, except by the few who had known him. Clover was an old stout（肥胖的） mare（母马） now, stiff in the joints and with a tendency（倾向） to rheumy eyes. She was two years past the retiring（退休） age, but no animal had ever actually retired（退休的）.

[P02] The talk of setting aside（旁边） a corner of the pasture（牧场） for superannuated（超龄的） animals had long since been dropped. Napoleon was now a mature（成熟的） boar（公猪） of twenty-four stone（石头）. Squealer was so fat that he could hardly see out of his eyes. Only old Benjamin was much the same as ever, except for being a little greyer about the muzzle（口鼻部）, and, since Boxer's death, more morose（郁郁寡欢的） and taciturn（沉默寡言的） than ever. There were many more creatures（生物） on the farm now, though the increase was not so great as expected. Many animals had been born to whom the uprising was only a dim（昏暗的） tradition, passed on by word of mouth, and others had been bought who had never heard of such a thing before they arrived.

[P03] The farm had three horses now besides Clover. They were fine, tall animals, willing workers and good comrades（同志们）, but very stupid. None could learn the alphabet（字母表） past the letter B. They accepted everything told about the uprising and Animalism（动物主义）, especially from Clover, whom they respected almost like a parent; but it was doubtful（怀疑的） whether they understood much. Many animals had been born to whom the uprising was only a dim tradition, passed on by word of mouth. The farm was more prosperous（繁荣的） now, and better organised: it had even been enlarged（放大的） by two fields bought from Mr. Pilkington.
